This should handle fresh snow pretty easily, but I could see the rubber brushless blades having trouble with more frozen ice/compact hard snow that has been sitting for hours overnight between the driveway and fresher fallen snow.

2 batteries for continuous use - comes 3/4 charged
Quiet operation and motor
Center Joystick makes adjusting throw direction/angle a breeze

Results.ReviewText: This unit is packed very well and mostly pre-assembled.  The only tool you will need to attached the two (2) piece handles, lever, and snow chute is a 10mm socket or phillips head screwdriver.  Includes two 40 volt batteries and one charger.  Each battery has a four light press to test charge status, and both can be housed inside the battery compartment on the snowblower and swapped when the first one is depleted. I have never had a snowblower that was not self propelled before but think this might work well if the snow is not very deep and will be much cleaner and easier to store that a heavier gasoline powered model.  I have over the years replaced my gas lawnmower, string trimmer, handheld leaf blower as well as backpack blower and power-washer with EGO electric units and will never go back to gas or gas/oil mix again!

Results.OriginalProductName: Cordless 40-volt 20-in Single-stage Push Battery Snow Blower (Battery Included) (Charger Included)
Results.ReviewText:
I must preface this with the fact that I got this before our first snowfall, so I can't really report on how it performs. But I can give feedback on what the unit entails, especially in comparison to two other battery  snowblowers I have.
I'll Start with the CONS: First,This item came with (2) batteries, and I had hopes that it would use both batteries, but the sneaky engineers created a place for both batteries but can only use one. The other slot is just for storage. With only 40v on hand, and a single battery, even at 4ah, I don't think this will get very far. 
Secondly, according to the manual, the expected usage is one hour of use, but the battery takes 2 hours to charge. 
Third, while the scraper bar is removable, which is nice, it is plastic and I'd imagine that this will wear away very quickly. 
Fourth, there is no speed control. It is only on or off. And the start button is on the side in a weird spot. I think it will be tough while you are wearing gloves. 
Fifth, the paddle does not go the width of the opening. there is a good 3-4 inches on either side that is just open and might clog up, or just not get flung out, effectively narrowing the unit.
Lastly, it is a very light machine in weight. That's nice to push around, but I don't know how long this will hold up, as it is mostly plastic and we'll see how well it lasts. 
On the PRO side: It is lightweight and easy to push around. 
Second, the rotation mechanism is fairly direct and easy to use. 
Last, the safety controls are easy to hold onto and the cross bar is at a good height.
Results.Title: Only uses a single battery and has design flaws

Results.ReviewText:
The instructions were clear and easy to follow, making the assembly process a breeze. I was impressed with the quality of the materials and construction of the snow thrower. It felt sturdy and well-built, giving me confidence that it would hold up well during use. Overall, I was very satisfied and excited to put my new Wild Badger snow thrower to the test during the next snowstorm. It only took me 15 minutes from the time I opened the box and had it completely assembled. Basically you have to attach the handle and screw down the snow chute.

Overall, the design of this snow thrower is incredibly user-friendly. The placement of the lever and chute adjustment bar make it convenient to control.  This attention to detail is surprising to me in such a reasonably priced 40 volt snow thrower. It is clear that a lot of thought went into making this machine as user-friendly as possible. 

This model comes with two 4ah batteries, one is used to run the snow thrower and the other fits right next to it for an easy swap if the first one runs out. 

The battery charger isn’t as intuitive as it could be. Only one of the LEDs blinks during charging. When it is finished, it stays on, but the other LED does not light up. After reading the manual closer, I saw that the other LED is red and only comes on if the battery temperature is too low or there is a malfunction. It wasn’t a big deal, just not like other chargers I have. On the plus side it charges the batteries very quickly!

It folds up nicely for storage and fits right under a shelf in my garage, unlike the gas snow thrower that this is replacing. This has a wider opening for the snow and the overall size is smaller.  
Can’t wait for it to snow now!
Results.Title: Easy to assemble and really well thought out

Results.OriginalProductName: Cordless 40-volt 20-in Single-stage Push Battery Snow Blower (Battery Included) (Charger Included)
Results.ReviewText:
This snow "thrower" is designed for small, paved driveways or areas. I was able to clear about a 30x35' area of 5" of snow per battery. Deeper snow will reduce the area you can clear. It was easy to assemble with a 3/8" and 10mm socket in about 10 minutes. At about 35# it's easy to lift and move around. It is not self propelled, so you have to push it through the snow and the handle is short forcing my 6'2" frame to stoop over while using it. It did throw the snow 15-20', so from the center of the driveway, most of the snow landed off the driveway. The shoot rotation control is quick and easy to rotate from side to side.

I did try using it on an area of gravel driveway and it tended to dig into the gravel and shoot it out. I saw no damage to the paddles, but I doubt that it would hold up to long term use over gravel. It was challenging to hold the front edge up above the gravel and I ended up with a bit over an inch of snow remaining. 

My biggest complaint with this unit is the batteries. They will not charge if they are too cold or hot. When I first received the unit and tried to charge the batteries they were at 35 degrees from being outside. It took them over an hour and a half to warm up in the 70 degree house before they would start charging. Then after discharging fully in about 10 minutes, they were hot and took about two hours to cool down enough in the 70 degree house to start the charging cycle. Charging took just over the stated 120 minutes to charge each battery. So if you discharge both batteries using it for 20 minutes, it will be over six hours before you have two recharged batteries to continue with.
Results.Title: Light Snow Thrower for Small Paved Driveway

Photos.Caption: Our sidewalk after going over it with the snowblower
The bottom front of the machine

Results.ReviewText: I unpacked it and set everything out. I was surprised at the amount of plastic parts. My biggest concern is how they will hold up when the weather gets below zero. Will they become brittle and break? We will find out this winter. The auger is made of hard rubber. The shoot is manually adjusted, and has several adjustment settings. On the bottom of the blower is a set of plastic high points. The blower does not get to ground level because of these high points. The batteries charge pretty quick, about 4 hours per battery. It comes with a charger and two batteries. I will see how the really cold weather treats the machine and its parts. If anything changes, I will add to the review this coming spring.
Results.Title: Badger Snowblower

Results.OriginalProductName: Cordless 40-volt 20-in Single-stage Push Battery Snow Blower (Battery Included) (Charger Included)
Results.ReviewText: This Wild Badger snow thrower comes with all the features you look for  in a great snow thrower. It’s so fast and easy to assemble too. Once fully assembled in 30-45 minutes max, one can really appreciate its features. It’s so easy to start by just pressing the safety button and then pulling down on the bail switch. To turn off just release the bail switch. The rubber paddle is 20 inches wide and can handle up to 10 inches of snow depth. It should also be able to throw the snow up to 25 feet thru its chute. The chute is able to rotate 180 degrees from left to right to discharge the snow using the chute rotation handle on the handle frame. The chute deflector handle on top of the main chute will adjust the snow discharge on a higher or lower trajectory. This unit also has a LED headlight in the front to lighten up the pathway during darker hours. Wild Badger gives you two battery packs that are placed inside the unit in its own compartment. One runs the snow thrower while this other is a backup when needed. Both are easy to put in and pull out. A charger unit is also contained for the batteries. Overall I’m very pleased with the Wild Badger Snow Thrower with all its features and ready to take on the next snowfall.

Results.OriginalProductName: Cordless 40-volt 20-in Single-stage Push Battery Snow Blower (Battery Included) (Charger Included)
Results.ReviewText: As lightweight as this snow blower is, it feels really solid.  It's easy to assemble (make sure you have your 10mm socket handy) and has some really well-designed features, such as a brushless motor, storage for a spare battery, flexible blades, and even a headlamp.  A push-button safety interlock means the toddlers aren't likely to fire it up.  It handles light to moderate snow pretty easily and runs fast enough to throw the snow a reasonable distance, even without a second stage.  The only drawback I found is that the batteries are of a proprietary design and not, as far as I can tell, compatible with any other manufacturer's products.
Results.Title: Another Cordless Toy!
